channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
item.description: Here the authors present ‘Sup-seq’, a transposon-based sequencing technique that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression in bacteria. They use it to identify 53 genetic suppressors of seven essential genes in pneumococcus, revealing new links among metabolism, ribosome assembly, and membrane lipid synthesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Live-cell 3D mapping reveals the organized architecture of FG-nucleoporins within the nuclear pore complex
item.description: 3D imaging in living cells reveals how nuclear pore FG-Nups organize: five central FG-Nups form a ring around a sparse axial corridor, while six asymmetric FG-Nups form dynamic caps, together directing diffusion and selective transport.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae
item.description: Bacterial cell division requires coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by FtsW and FtsI. Here, authors uncover that conformational switching of FtsI, via a coupling helix, spatiotemporally links glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking.

item.title: Nature Communications: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
item.description: DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
item.description: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

item.title: Nature Communications: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
item.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a global pathogen of public health importance; however, the mechanisms underlying virulence and antimicrobial resistance remain poorly understood. Here, the authors used a systematic pan-genome approach to identify conserved regulatory features across bacterial strains providing new insights into pathogenicity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.description: Gallstone disease is common, but its genetic basis remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors conduct a trans‑ancestry GWAS identifying 116 risk loci, linking gallstone susceptibility to lipid and liver metabolism pathways and expanding understanding of disease biology across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
item.description: Here, the authors show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O-antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae and that this surface-remodeling adaptation enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
item.description: Long-term CO 2 -generated declines in ocean pH block recycling of silicon, an essential nutrient for diatom-driven ocean production. Associated reductions in chlorophyll and plankton-feeding fish reveal a novel CO 2 impact on marine ecosystem health.

item.title: Nature Communications: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
item.description: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) silences one of the two X chromosomes in females, but its role in human development is unclear. Here, the authors show that human extraembryonic differentiation triggers XIST-dependent XCI, important for cell survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: Blood p-tau217 is a leading Alzheimer’s test but is also raised in ALS. Here, the authors show that muscle makes its own form of tau which leaks into the blood, and that detecting brain-derived p-tau217 improves the test’s accuracy.

Nature Communications: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
item.description: While sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics has reached subcellular resolution, its low capture efficiency compromises downstream analysis. Here, authors present a spatial transcriptomic platform that achieves ~1μm resolution with substantially enhanced capture efficiency.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
item.description: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is an aggressive lung cancer whose biological diversity remains poorly understood. Here, the authors combine genomic, epigenomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses to show that LCNEC cells can shift between neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine states, identifying intermediate cell states and immune microenvironment features that may influence prognosis and treatment responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
item.description: PRMT5 is essential for cell proliferation, but the basis for this requirement is unclear. Here, the authors show that PRMT5 sustains histone transcription and genome integrity and identify H4R3me2s at histone locus bodies, linking H4 arginine methylation to cellular histone homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage
item.description: DNA is a dense and durable storage medium for digital information but its use in living cells remains difficult to scale and protect. Here, authors present DNA CODEC, a CRISPR-based system that distributes compressed data across engineered cell populations for stable storage and controlled access.

item.title: Nature Communications: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
item.description: Lipids can influence membrane proteins through distinct regulatory mechanisms. Here, Newton et al. reveal that lipid concentration determines whether an anionic phospholipid acts as a specific allosteric regulator or a general membrane modulator within the same protein system.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
item.description: Authors present a global study revealing that drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae repeatedly acquires conjugative plasmids with aerobactin, boosting iron-scavenging ability without becoming hypervirulent. This may help emerging strains spread in healthcare settings.

item.title: Nature Communications: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal–dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing
item.description: Biomaterials are widely used in wound care, but whether they can actively direct tissue repair remains not well understood. Here, authors show that silk fibroin intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a regenerative state that coordinates epidermal–dermal crosstalk and promotes wound healing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions
item.description: Gap junction channels assemble into plaques that coordinate communication across tissues. Here, authors show how neighboring Cx46/50 channels pack within membranes and identify ordered lipids as major components of their interfaces

item.title: Nature Communications: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates
item.description: While PARP inhibitors are well characterized, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition are undefined. Here, the authors propose a unified mechanism in which the sequestration of PAR-binding proteins underlies PARG inhibitor-induced cytotoxicity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes
item.description: Horizontal gene transfer may shape how lichen symbionts adapt, but its role remains unclear. Across 197 lichen MAGs, this study identified 1,882 putative horizontally transferred genes and 31 potential transfers between fungal and algal symbionts, with distinct functional patterns.

item.title: Nature Communications: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis
item.description: Identifying ligand-binding proteins and determining their affinities is important but challenging in complex systems. Here, the authors develop 2D-PELSA, a peptide-centric, dose-resolved method for target identification and local affinity estimation and reveal an E2-GPX4 link to ferroptosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
item.description: This study reveals how persistent TFE3 activation triggers the neurodevelopmental disorder TFE3-NDD by disrupting critical cellular functions, including energy production, lysosomal function, and cell-matrix interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
item.description: Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
item.description: Here, by analyzing nearly 5,000 gut microbiomes, the authors show that inflammation in IBD is associated with the loss of beneficial bacteria, increased microbial community instability, and reduced persistence of bacterial strains, suggesting that inflammation may not only disrupt the gut microbiome but also limit its ability to recover, providing a potential explanation for the persistence of dysbiosis in IBD.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation
item.description: Mitochondrial protein synthesis can stall at difficult-to-translate sequences. Here, authors combine cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling and MD simulations to show how TACO1 engages the mitoribosome and A-site tRNA to support translation elongation.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
item.description: Cell Painting captures the internal organization of cells, but until now has been mostly confined to flat monolayers. Here, authors extend Cell Painting to single cells within 3D spheroids, demonstrating that drug responses which are alike in 2D cultures diverge within 3D cultures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
item.description: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Here the authors genetically engineer the moss, Physcomitrium patens , for de novo paclitaxel biosynthesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: IRAK4 autophosphorylation functions as a molecular switch to regulate death domain assembly and Myddosome maturation
item.description: Inflammatory signalling depends on higher-order protein assemblies such as the Myddosome. Here, authors show that IRAK4 autophosphorylation is a molecular switch that relieves IRAK1/2/3 autoinhibition, driving Myddosome maturation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
item.description: Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
item.description: Restricting branched-chain amino acids is linked to metabolic benefits. Here, the authors show that valine directly binds ATP5F1B in cardiac tissue from hypertensive male rodents, and that low-valine diet stabilizes this protein by reducing LONP1-mediated degradation.

item.title: Nature Communications: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
item.description: Genomic-based tests for Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. Here, the authors find that the multi-model transformer-based method HRDPath could be used as a digital biomarker to improve ovarian cancer diagnosis and therapy selection.’

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
item.description: This study shows that tracking tumor DNA in blood can help predict outcomes, monitor treatment response, and reveal resistance in women receiving bireociclib plus fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
item.description: Analysis of 1.35 million emergency department visits found that racial and ethnic disparities in triage scores were concentrated in lower-risk visits, where assessment relies more on clinical judgment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
item.description: This trial demonstrates the safety of sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive therapy in severe malaria in African children and identified, using a continual reassessment method design, the optimal dose to investigate in future trials.

item.title: Nature Communications: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
item.description: How different biodegradable plastics break down within landfills, particularly landfill leachate, remain unclear. Here, they evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), using a combination of genome-resolved multi-omics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
item.description: Lipid accumulation in solid tumors supports tumor progression by promoting immune evasion. Yet the molecular basis of this lipid-mediated immunosuppression remains unclear. Here, using murine models of advanced colorectal cancer, the authors uncover a metabolic-immune axis whereby tumor-derived fatty acids activate neutrophil PPARα, resulting in adenosine generation and T cell suppression. Importantly, treatment with a dual adenosine receptor antagonist restores T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance animal survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development
item.description: Wang et al . apply single particle cryo-EM to developing gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum , and identify human hemoglobin as a prominent factor that binds to P. falciparum subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network.

item.title: Nature Communications: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism
item.description: The mechanisms underlying social behavioural deficits in mouse models of autism are not fully understood. Here the authors link neural embedding geometry to context-dependent social deficits in the Shank3 knockout mouse.

item.title: Nature Communications: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
item.description: Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing, authors show Eilat virus has abundant deletion-type defective viral genomes; delineating it from other arthropod-borne alphaviruses. This is likely driven by low replicase processivity and premature termination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction
item.description: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) is often slow growing, but a subset of tumors can be aggressive. Here, the authors profile tumors from 797 PTC patients to define six molecular subtypes, identify protein markers linked to low- and high-risk disease, and develop a proteomic classification framework that may improve risk stratification and treatment decisions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
item.description: ACSS1 mediates maladaptive mitonuclear communication under nutrient stress, impairing metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis. Targeting ACSS1 preserves bone integrity in diabetic and alcoholic mice by sustaining bone formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
item.description: The KARI dataset maps healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease across >6,000 scans from 1,645 adults. Demonstrating its utility, imaging biomarkers scale with clinical severity, providing a resource to accelerate future Alzheimer research.

item.title: Nature Communications: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
item.description: Defective clearance of senescent cells contributes to chronic systemic inflammation and tissue damage. Here, the authors adopt a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence and report that oncogenic signal strength and the adaptive immune response govern senescent cell clearance, ultimately influencing animal survival

item.title: Nature Communications: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
item.description: Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
item.description: Here, the authors report the identification and characterization of large, up to 1.58 million base-pair-long plasmids in gut microbiomes worldwide, showing that while most genes remain uncharacterized, these plasmids are linked to E. coli and Shigella isolates and can greatly expand host function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma develops within a complex tissue environment, but the factors that initiate tumor formation are not fully understood. Here, the authors identify tumor-associated peripheral glial cells as drivers of tumor initiation, showing that they promote pro-tumor macrophage activation and stromal changes required for early cancer development.

item.title: Nature Communications: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
item.description: Overgeneralizing aversive memories to safe contexts is a feature of stress-related disorders. Here, authors show that a prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls the specificity of aversive memories independently of glucocorticoids.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation
item.description: Inflammation and recovery from ulcerative colitis (UC) involves various immune cells and mediators. Here the authors examine the function of NFκB using patient samples and reporter mice to show that NFκB promotes T regulatory cell recruitment through CCL22 and a propensity towards repair.

item.title: Nature Communications: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury
item.description: Radiotherapy for lung cancer often induces radiation-induced lung injury (RILI). Here, the authors analyze innate lymphoid cells (ILC) in a RILI mouse model, finding that radiation-induced type I interferon directs ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity, and inhibition of type I interferon signaling reduces ILC plasticity and RILI.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference
item.description: Here the authors present a chromosome-level Emirati pangenome, capturing population-specific genetic diversity and improving the detection of genomic variants. The resource will support more accurate genetic research and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
item.description: A study of 2,536 MDR Salmonella genomes across China’s food chain forecasts resistance to 2050. Antibiotic use and population growth associate with rising carbapenem and colistin resistance, with food workers an overlooked last-resort ARG reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: G-quadruplex structures affect the immune response to bacterial infection in mouse macrophages
item.description: G-quadruplexes (G4) are dynamic nucleic acid structures regulating various cellular functions. Here, the authors show that G4 formation sterically inhibits NF-κB-driven activation of pro-inflammatory genes, such as Il1b, acting as structural checkpoint to limit macrophage inflammatory responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
item.description: Cheng et al. characterize two bacterial anti-phage systems that act via either protease-mediated cleavage or kinase-dependent phosphorylation to target phage tail-fiber proteins, establishing the concept passive abortive infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
item.description: Macrophages tightly control their phagocytic capacity, limiting intracellular overcrowding. However, the molecular details of this adaptive response remain undefined. Here, the authors combine live in vivo imaging with fly genetics and show that, in phagocytic Drosophila macrophages, mechanical and molecular adaptations of the nucleus to the indenting phagosomal cargoes are required to sustain macrophage phagocytosis in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
item.description: Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

item.title: Nature Communications: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
item.description: CDK11 encodes a poorly-characterized cyclin-dependent kinase. Here, the authors demonstrate that CDK11 is essential for cancer proliferation, but the function(s) of CDK11 in normal tissue limits the efficacy of CDK11 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD + hydrolysis
item.description: Nucleotide signals activate bacterial immune defenses against phages. Here, authors show that dITP activates the Kongming system by shifting protein assemblies toward a catalytically active state

item.title: Nature Communications: Towards scalable DNA data storage with DNA-SaM codec system
item.description: Scaling DNA storage is limited by complex codecs, biochemically problematic sequences, and insufficient architecture for large-scale data. Here, the authors present DNA-SaM, integrating efficient encoding, biochemical checks, and a storage unit distribution with a two-tiered indexing architecture.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
item.description: Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT
item.description: This study introduces microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomics method that maps host and bacterial RNA together in gut tissue, revealing how microbes and host responses vary across intestinal regions and during inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
item.description: Here the authors present RASSCCoL, a rapid physics-based method for designing small-molecule-binding proteins. It yields robust binders for a range of fluorophores to enable controlled energy transfer and live-cell imaging.

item.title: Nature Communications: A prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system that prevents DNA packaging by targeting the terminase complex
item.description: Some temperate phages protect their host bacteria from a second phage infection. Here, the authors show that a prophage encodes an anti-phage defence system, which inhibits packaging of invading phage DNA, and self-immunity proteins that enable the resident prophage to propagate

item.title: Nature Communications: Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
item.description: The authors develop a high-throughput assay to identify small molecule RIG-I agonists. Using this assay, they identify and optimize a class of agonists, including one that induces interferon signaling across multiple cell types.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mosquito repellency mediated by skin commensal Bacillus species via volatile metabolite reprogramming
item.description: Why some people get bitten by mosquitoes more than others has been a long-standing question. Here, the authors uncover specific chemical compounds produced by two resident skin microbes that, when applied to animals, reduce their “attractiveness” to mosquitoes and increases repellent time.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
item.description: A quarter of the world’s freshwater fish species are used for food, recreation, or ornamental purposes. These species harbour unique morphologies, many threatened, whose loss would erode irreplaceable ecological strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte
item.description: The authors find that the live-attenuated cholera vaccine CVD 103-HgR was 87% effective during the 2024 Mayotte outbreak, averting several hundred cases. Live-attenuated vaccines could complement killed vaccines amid global shortages.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
item.description: Using large-scale plasma proteomics, Kim et al. identify proteins altered in ALS and develop a 10-protein model with high classification accuracy, supporting development of a blood-based tool to facilitate earlier ALS diagnosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
item.description: Most covalent organic framework photosensitizers are activated by UV or visible light, limiting tissue penetration and reducing effectiveness against deep-seated tumours. The authors engineered a metal-free, near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin COF that generates ROS and heat under 808 nm irradiation, inducing immunogenic cell death and achieving strong suppression of 4T1 and CT26 tumours.

item.title: Nature Communications: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
item.description: Insulin resistance in skeletal muscle contributes to type 2 diabetes (T2D), but its causes remain unclear. We identify the mitochondrial protein Miro1 as a key regulator of muscle insulin sensitivity, providing new insights into T2D development.

item.title: Nature Communications: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
item.description: In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: This study shows complementary roles of plasma p-tau217 and eMTBRtau243 across Alzheimer’s disease, supporting their use for blood-based assessment of tau pathology, biological staging and prognosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
item.description: This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
item.description: Here the authors demonstrate that interactions between Bacteroides and Escherichia shape resistance to Clostridioides difficile and identify ecological and metabolic signatures with the potential to guide microbiome-based therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular basis of PADI6 species-specific oligomerization in maternal regulatory complexes
item.description: Maternal effector PADI6 forms the MPU complex with UHRF1 and UBE2D and assembles CPLs with SCMC members in oocytes and early embryos. PADI6’s oligomerization capacity, driven by its N-terminal domain, defines species-specific MPU structure and highlights differences in CPL architecture and regulatory mechanisms

item.title: Nature Communications: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
item.description: Here, the authors map antibody responses to Epstein-Barr virus protein regions, identifying signatures associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma detection, chemotherapy response and progression-free survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
item.description: Graspetides are ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides. Here, TIGR04500 family proteins are shown to guide graspetide biosynthesis as non-catalytic chaperone-like partners through a likely widespread recognition mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: Coordinated control of both microtubule ends regulates mitotic spindle length
item.description: Length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends facilitates the coordinated action of plus- and minus-end dynamics, explaining how mitotic spindle length is maintained in systems with poleward flux.

item.title: Nature Communications: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition
item.description: As proteomics experiments grow in scale, poor-quality measurements are increasingly hard to detect yet undermine biological conclusions. Here, the authors introduce MSstats + , a method that uses peak quality metrics and their temporal profiles to downweight poor measurements in differential analysis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
item.description: In this study, the authors benchmark four wastewater sequencing methods for influenza A, including two that were developed in-house. Using a custom probe panel they recover H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1, including H5N1 signals when dPCR was limited.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary extensions of IF2 couple translation initiation to bacterial stress adaptation
item.description: Translation initiation factor 2 (IF2) is a universally conserved component of the protein synthesis machinery. Here, Fer et al. show that IF2 terminal extensions couple translation initiation to stress adaptation, highlighting a mechanism by which evolutionary expansion of core proteins enables regulatory flexibility in changing environments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
item.description: Chen and colleagues present scMagnify, a framework that uses single-cell multi-omic data to reconstruct and decompose time-lagged gene regulatory networks. The study analyses regulatory programs associated with development and disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
item.description: Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes.

item.title: Nature Communications: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
item.description: Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
item.description: In cognitively normal individuals, the rate of change in concentrations of plasma ptau217 and Aβ−42/40 over age differs between APOE ε4 carriers and non-carriers. For p-tau217, the effect of APOE ε4 carriership is stronger in males than females.

item.title: Nature Communications: Brown adipose tissue ankyrin-B cell-autonomously modulates lipid content and its deletion protects male mice against diet-induced obesity
item.description: Ankyrin-B couples BAT lipid droplet lipolysis to thermogenic fuel availability. Its loss impairs thermoregulation during fasting but preserves fed-state thermogenesis and protects against diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
item.description: Authors present their chain-as-prompt deep learning framework, which identifies antimicrobial lipopeptides that show efficacy against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens in laboratory and animal model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
item.description: CDK4/6 inhibitors can trigger stress responses that alter tumor outcomes. Here, the authors show that PERK signaling shapes cell fate after CDK4/6 inhibition and influences response to therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans
item.description: The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is linked to cognitive control and is thought to generate the reward positivity (RewP), a brain signal reflecting outcomes versus expectations. Here, the authors show, in 68 stroke patients, that damage to the caudal ACC selectively reduced the RewP, providing causal evidence that this region generates the signal.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CRC–MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis
item.description: Flowers produce nectar in specialized organs called nectaries, but how these organs acquire their size remains unclear. Here, the authors show that a DNA loop coordinates gene activity and hormone transport to control nectary size in Arabidopsis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
item.description: Structural isomers can be difficult to distinguish and map by mass alone. This study shows that Orbitrap-SIMS can separate and image isomeric sugars directly on surfaces, offering a new route to study complex biomolecules.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
item.description: Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration
item.description: Here they use spatial transcriptomics to analyze cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells in zebrafish heart and show that adrenomedullin a and ackr3a are critical in cardiac lymphatic vessel development and immune cell clearance during regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLH MKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
item.description: The CTLH MKLN1 E3 ligase recruits diverse substrates but the underlying mechanisms were unclear. Here, the authors use cryo-EM, biochemistry, and cellular experiments to show how MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains combinatorially recognize internal, Arg/C-, and Ac/N-degrons across distinct substrates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB
item.description: In a Lesotho cohort treated with a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB, baseline chest radiographic features (cavities, fibrosis, bilateral disease) and high sputum smear grade, individually and in-combination, predicted slower sputum clearance and increased risk for poor outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
item.description: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, the authors found that short-term, low-dose perioperative glucocorticoids may improve cerebrovascular outcomes as an adjunct to flow diverter therapy for unruptured intracranial aneurysms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
item.description: Anti-CRISPR proteins inhibit bacterial CRISPR immunity, but how auxiliary structural elements enhance inhibition is unclear. Here, authors show that an extended AcrIIC1 loop supports HNH-domain engagement and modulates sgRNA positioning and R-loop formation to strengthen Cas9 inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Viral SSB-bound ssDNA activates the bacterial anti-phage defense system DARNA
item.description: Bacteria use various defense systems to protect themselves against phage infection, but their activation mechanisms are often unclear. Here, the authors show that the anti-viral system DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage protein SSB, leading to host tRNA cleavage and inhibition of phage propagation.

item.title: Nature Communications: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface
item.description: The study reveals how the antiviral protein MxB recognizes and binds the HIV-1 capsid, uncovering a distinct binding mechanism that may inform strategies for targeting HIV.

item.title: Nature Communications: ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 amplifies ILC2 activation and allergic lung inflammation
item.description: IL-33 is known to promote differentiation and activation of innate lymphoid cells type 2 (ILC2). Here the authors show that IL-33 generated by ILC2 has a function in the increase of inflammatory allergic responses and can be promoted by exogenous IL-33 and cysteinyl leukotrienes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
item.description: Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
item.description: This study shows that microRNA-200 blocks sebaceous gland formation by activating WNT signaling, suppressing SOX9-dependent lipid metabolic programs and limiting proliferation. These findings reveal how epithelial cell fate is spatially regulated during skin development.

item.title: Nature Communications: LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning
item.description: LitGene is an interpretable AI model that learns gene representations from scientific text and Gene Ontology, enabling zero-shot prediction of gene functions and disease links; it reveals ANGPTL6 as a candidate gene in pulmonary fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A mouse neuroimmune circuit that regulates allergic inflammation in the esophagus
item.description: The allergic disease eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is often accompanied by refractory pain, but how neuroimmune crosstalk impacts EoE remains unclear. Here, the authors show, using mouse models of allergic inflammation, that allergen exposure increases esophageal innervation and alters sensitivity of sensory neurons, identifying a potential feedforward loop for amplifying inflammation and causing pain.

item.title: Nature Communications: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
item.description: Training physical neural networks remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here the authors engineer E. coli with memregulons to implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
item.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction can occur without obesity. Here, the authors show that it is common in Japanese cohorts and find in mice that hypertensive stress alters macrophage signaling, promoting metabolic remodeling and inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fluke-borne viruses are a risk factor and diagnostic target for diseases caused by carcinogenic trematodes
item.description: Authors discovered that cancer-causing parasitic flukes carry their own viruses and shed some of them. They show that antibody titers and avidity to the fluke viruses predict liver fibrosis and bile-duct cancer risk, and that serologies could be used as prognostic biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study
item.description: Apelin can counteract water retention and may help correct low blood sodium. Here, the authors show in a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial that intravenous apelin does not meaningfully increase urine output in adults with experimentally induced hyponatremia.

item.title: Nature Communications: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries
item.description: This study of over 100,000 pregnancies in four European countries found that both initial and booster COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy were linked to lower risks of infection and related hospital admission.

item.title: Nature Communications: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
item.description: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
item.description: Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking.

item.title: Nature Communications: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization
item.description: How epithelial-derived ITLN1 shapes neutrophil immunity in colorectal cancer remains unclear. The authors here show that ITLN1 promotes STAT3/C/EBPδ-associated neutrophil maturation and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, linking bone marrow granulopoiesis to mature-neutrophil spatial organization and anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration
item.description: This study identifies IL-18 as an inflammatory switch that drives macrophage dysfunction and impairs stem cell function, thereby limiting skeletal regeneration and revealing a potential therapeutic target for bone repair.

item.title: Nature Communications: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
item.description: The identification of clinically relevant driver alterations in prostate cancer remains elusive. Here, integrative analysis of cancer driver genes using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1,001 men identifies four oncotypes, two of which are associated with poor clinical outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
item.description: Aisyah et al. report nationwide use of Indonesia’s integrated ASIK-SATUSEHAT system for 116 million NCD screening visits, showing broad primary-care adoption alongside variation by service, region, age and sex.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
item.description: In this study, Slavov et al. identify MWPyV DNA in 7.7% of pediatric oropharyngeal samples from Brazil, predominantly in young children and at low viral loads. Genomic analyses reveal distinct viral lineages and evidence of recombination, while electron microscopy provides ultrastructural evidence of MWPyV particles in respiratory specimens.

item.title: Nature Communications: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
item.description: Dietary exposure to nanoplastics is an emerging health concern. Here, the authors show that high-fiber diet reduces nanoplastic gastrointestinal retention, alleviates intestinal injury, and limits organ translocation in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
item.description: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multiorgan injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that USP28 deubiquitinates NMMHC IIA to enhance IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling, thereby driving endothelial necroptosis in sepsis in a male mouse model of sepsis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
item.description: The authors develop MRZ, a Mendelian randomization method that models variant-outcome z-scores as a mixture to separate causal effects from pleiotropy, and validate the causal findings in mouse experiments.

item.title: Nature Communications: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
item.description: The mechanisms driving early axonal and synaptic dysfunction in ALS remain unclear. Here, the authors identify compartment-specific RNA changes and identify SLITRK2 as a driver of axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS using an iNMJ-on-a-chip model.

item.title: Nature Communications: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
item.description: Macrophage pyroptosis has been shown to be involved in acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors find that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) is downregulated in AKI and that loss of RNF130 in myeloid cells aggravates renal pathological damage and that RNF130 decreases macrophage pyroptosis through prevention of ubiquitination and inactivation of PDCD4 and that otherwise PDCD4 promotes phosphorylation of NF-kB and STAT3 leading to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and macrophage pyroptosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
item.description: Here, Garcia-Prieto et al use spatial transcriptomics to reveal progressive endothelial, pneumocyte type I and natural killer cell loss, expansion of myeloid and stromal cells, TGF-β-driven fibrosis signaling and alveolar regeneration programs in fatal COVID-19 lung injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: Klebsiella -dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
item.description: Here, the authors identify a relationship between rotavirus vaccine response, colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, and inflammation across a cohort of infants from three different regions (Panama, Peru, and the U.S.A).’

item.title: Nature Communications: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
item.description: Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: Here the authors analyse mobility and COVID-19 data from 122 countries to examine how changes in movement affected virus transmission. They find that mobility data improved estimates of SARS-CoV-2 spread, particularly in Western Europe and North America.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
item.description: In this randomized controlled trial, authors show that sodium zirconium cyclosilicate helped people with heart failure and chronic kidney disease reach recommended doses of key heart failure medicines, while reducing episodes of high blood potassium without added safety concerns.

item.title: Nature Communications: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
item.description: Researchers linked four Fitbit-derived activity measures, from step count to cadence, to over 400 diseases in 29,303 adults, revealing new associations with conditions including chronic pain and autoimmune disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
item.description: Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
item.description: The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
item.description: Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

item.title: Nature Communications: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
item.description: Using single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, researchers showed the four-eyed fish Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of its ventral retina and regional opsin gene tuning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
item.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced myocarditis is a rare side effect of ICI therapy. Here the authors use multi-omics approaches to characterize the immune cells and mediators involved and find monocytes and ISG15 + CD8 + T cells as well as an 8-protein panel to better distinguish ICI-myocarditis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
item.description: In this study authors showcase a rabbit-to-human translational model that predicts anti-tuberculosis drug distribution in patient lesions and effectively discerns Phase 3 regimen outcomes, helping to design more robust strategies for regimen prioritization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
item.description: Time-restricted eating and structured exercise training have both been reported to reduce hepatic steatosis and improve cardiometabolic profile. Here the authors report a randomized controlled trial showing that in adults with obesity, time-restricted eating, supervised exercise, or their combination did not reduce intrahepatic fat more than usual care that consisted of Mediterranean diet and physical activity education.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
item.description: Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
item.description: This study reports that the circular RNA BRAKE is a mitochondria-localized regulator of adipogenesis. By disrupting ATP synthase assembly, circRNA BRAKE restrains adipocyte differentiation and contributes to metabolic dysfunction during obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
item.description: Origin-destination data on air travel are essential for studying global mobility and epidemic risk but are often proprietary. Here, authors introduce a maximum-entropy network method that reconstructs air passenger flows from open data and enables accurate reproduction of epidemic dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: An international multicenter study of MASLD prevalence among children and adolescents assessed by VCTE
item.description: A multicenter study in 17 countries on pediatric MASLD, a liver disorder, finds a prevalence of 18% in community populations and 58% in hospital populations, differences between regions, associations with obesity and elevated liver enzyme levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
item.description: BPL-1357 has shown broad protection in animal models against influenza viruses. The authors demonstrate safety of the vaccine given intramuscularly or intranasally in healthy adults in a phase I trial and characterize the elicited immune responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment
item.description: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing behavior remains largely unquantified because existing monitoring approaches cannot capture the distributed micro-contact dynamics within the bristle field. Here, the authors report DigiDent, a hardware-software co-designed framework combining embedded co-deformation sensing with AI-based analysis to quantify contact-rich brushing behavior. Pilot human studies demonstrate its potential for real-world brushing monitoring, personalized feedback, and habit assessment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Ki-67 governs the mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP). Here, authors identify the MCP as an AML vulnerability. NPM1c+ poorly loads onto the MCP, forms mitotic aggregates, delaying nucleolar entry. Ki-67 overexpression restores NPM1c+ nucleolar return.

item.title: Nature Communications: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
item.description: The Whole Blood Transcriptome database comprises data from 4,444 individuals with 98 distinct health conditions and matched plasma proteomics data from 1,280 with 28 health conditions, allowing identification of signatures of the conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
item.description: Transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms regulate responses to cytokines, as well as the crosstalk between pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines. Here, the authors demonstrate that pro-inflammatory TNF amplifies, rather than blocks, the anti-inflammatory IL-4 response in human monocytes and that NF-κB and STAT6 cooperate on chromatin to activate tissue-repair genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
item.description: RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
item.description: Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
item.description: Disparities in cancer diagnosis amongst patients with disabilities remains a challenge, yet there are limited European population-based studies addressing such issue. Here, the authors show that in Northern Italy, people with disabilities, particularly those with mental and neuromuscular impairments are more likely to be diagnosed with non-metastatic cancers following emergency presentation and also have a higher one-year mortality rate compared to those without impairments.

item.title: Nature Communications: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
item.description: Zhang et al. show that PRPF19 promotes hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis by driving PKM2-dependent glycolytic reprogramming, identifying a potential metabolic target in chronic liver disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-omics profiling uncovers diagnostic biomarker panel, progression-associated subtypes, and prognostic signature in pediatric mitochondrial disease
item.description: Pediatric mitochondrial disease lacks reliable biomarkers. Here, the authors show that a multi-omics study identified a 7-feature diagnostic panel (AUC = 0.96), revealed two proteomic subtypes with differing outcomes, and developed a 12-transcript prognostic signature (AUC = 0.85).

item.title: Nature Communications: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics reveals fibroblast and neuroimmune microenvironments in endometriosis lesions
item.description: Haney et al. map human endometriosis lesions and reveal shared cellular organization across endometriosis lesion types, identifying fibroblast compartments, neuro-immune interactions, and painsensing neurons, modeled in 3D co-culture systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
item.description: First generation inhibitors of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) had limited selectivity due to the conserved ATP binding pocket, resulting in toxicity when used as anti-cancer agent. Here, the authors report the results of a first-in-human clinical trial of Roginolisib, a next generation conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor, in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer with dose expansion in patients with metastatic uveal melanoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ethnicity, genomic ancestry, and HBV genotype in off-treatment outcomes following nucleos(t)ide analogue cessation: a prospective multicentre trial (COIN-B)
item.description: Authors show that after stopping hepatitis B therapy, off-treatment outcomes were linked to viral genotype and genomic ancestry rather than conventional ethnicity. Biologically grounded, granular patient characterization may help identify who can safely stop treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOE2 attenuates APOE4 -associated amyloid pathology and related toxicity in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Chen and colleagues use a heterozygous mouse model carrying human APOE2 and APOE4 alleles to show that APOE2 attenuates APOE4- associated effects on brain amyloid pathology and related cellular and molecular changes.

item.title: Nature Communications: SWI/SNF subunit SMARCD1 deficiency promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression via mitochondrial reprogramming
item.description: The SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex is associated with cancer. Here, the authors report that the SWI/SNF subunit SMARCD1 is a tumor suppressor in clear cell renal cell carcinoma through regulation of mitochondrial function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systematic comparison of affinity plasma proteomic technologies across multiple cohorts reveals generalizability of proteomic prediction
item.description: Proteomic prediction models often fail to transfer across cohorts and assay platforms. Here, the authors compare two leading proteomic technologies across 11 cohorts, identifying reliable proteins and correlation thresholds that yield more generalizable disease prediction models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Meta-analysis of empirical evidence on biodiversity and the risk of asthma
item.description: Biodiversity loss is associated with several adverse health effects. Here, the authors report the results of a meta-analysis investigating the effect of exposure to high environmental and human biodiversity on the risk of asthma.

item.title: Nature Communications: FMT combined with atezolizumab-bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma refractory to immunotherapy: an open label, single-arm, phase II pilot study
item.description: In this open label, single-arm, phase II pilot study, the authors report that fecal microbiota transplantation combined with atezolizumab/bevacizumab is safe and associates with a high response rate in patients with atezolizumab/bevacizumab-refractory hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Claudin-2 protects from enteropathogenic E. coli -infection and colitis by promoting crypt fetalization via β1-integrin/FAK/YAP signaling
item.description: Claudin-2 protects against EPEC-like infection and resultant colitis by promoting crypt fetalization through β1-integrin-FAKYAP signaling, identifying an important mechanism that coordinates mucosal repair, and host defense.

item.title: Nature Communications: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment
item.description: Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs remains a challenge. Here, the authors report that Treg expression of SATB1 distinguishes pro-tumorigenic Tregs from Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neonatal overfeeding accelerates age-related sarcopenia and metabolic disorders through lifelong gut mucosa and microbiota programming in mice
item.description: Here, the authors demonstrate that neonatal overfeeding in mice shortens lifespan and accelerates late-life muscle loss. This originates from persistent gut mucus defects and depleted Akkermansia muciniphila, revealing a targetable developmental origin for sarcopenia.

item.title: Nature Communications: EP300 inhibition alleviates acute-on-chronic liver failure through modulation of scar-associated macrophages
item.description: Acute-on-chronic liver failure is a life-threatening condition with limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that EP300 inhibition improves disease outcomes by enhancing the antibacterial function of scar-associated macrophages through ACOD1-dependent reprogramming.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clonal haematopoiesis subtypes confer dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection
item.description: Fewings et al. show that clonal haematopoiesis confers subtype- and dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection, with splicing-factor mutations carrying the greatest hazard, validated across five biobank cohorts totalling 889,215 individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy: a phase II clinical randomized trial
item.description: The authors reported a randomized trial showing that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD
item.description: Here, the authors show that unstable airway microbial communities and their interactions with the immune system are linked to airway inflammation in people with HIV and COPD.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale metagenomic characterization of the vaginal microbiome and uropathogens in women with recent bacterial vaginosis and urinary tract infections
item.description: Here, the authors characterize shotgun vaginal metagenomic profiles from women across the US in relation to recent history of bacterial vaginosis and urinary tract infections, revealing the vagina as a reservoir for uropathogens.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gastrointestinal tract delivery of hydrogen by dynamic gas-releasing frameworks
item.description: Hydrogen therapy is limited by efficient storage and controlled release. Here, the authors show that gas-releasing frameworks enable high-capacity, sustained intestinal H 2 delivery for management of multiple inflammatory disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis
item.description: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) can provide important benefits to childhood cancer patients, but clinical WGS workflows typically take weeks. Here, the authors evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of a rapid WGS research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics, reducing the mean turnaround time from 42 to 3 days without sacrificing the detection of clinically actionable variants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk
item.description: By integrating proteomics, genetics and imaging, this study identifies candidate blood biomarkers of pulmonary hypertension, implicates NOTCH3 in disease development, and defines distinct biological subtypes of individuals at risk for this condition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
item.description: Decentralized diagnostics has the potential to improve health equity as well as support a more rapid response to disease outbreaks. Here authors present SID-WAVES, a multimodal microfluidic platform which allows ‘sample-in, results-out’ detection of both nucleic acid and protein biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantifying parks as preventive health assets using population-scale mobility data
item.description: Using mobile-phone data from Greater Tokyo, the authors find that parks generate measurable walking-related health benefits, but returns vary widely. Smaller neighborhood parks often offer stronger investment potential than large destination parks.

item.title: Nature Communications: A randomized controlled trial of CDK7 inhibitor samuraciclib plus fulvestrant in advanced HR+/HER2− breast cancer
item.description: CDK7 is a therapeutic target in HR+/HER2- breast cancer due to its role in both cell cycle regulation and Estrogen Receptor transcription and activation. Here, the authors report a phase 2 randomised trial comparing samuraciclib (CDK7 inhibitor) plus fulvestrant (selective estrogen receptor degrader) against fulvestrant alone in patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer previously treated with CDK4/6 inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benchmarking imputation methods on real-world clinical time series with simulated spatio-temporal missingness
item.description: This work proposes a model to simulate complex missingness structures in clinical data. When applying various imputation methods to fill gaps of missing data, simple linear models are more robust than complex deep learning techniques.

item.title: Nature Communications: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
item.description: Low throughput and extensive data processing in current proteomic workflows hinder rapid sample classification. Here, the authors introduce a deep-learning approach that directly accepts mass spectrometry-derived peptide ion profiles to rapidly classify cell states or patient disease status.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
item.description: Feasibility and safety profile of intratumoral administration of a DC vaccine overexpressing CCL21 (CCL21-DC) have been previously reported in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here the authors report safety, clinical outcomes and immunological correlates of a phase I trial of CCL21-DC in combination with anti-PD1 pembrolizumab in patients with advanced NSCLC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
item.description: A multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform was established by conjugating NA inhibitors and Fc domain. AVCs cross-link flu viruses, blocking entry and release. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate outperformed clinical drugs in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
item.description: In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.
